items.title: Iran's nuclear timeline unchanged despite war, US intel finds

featured_image.name: Satellite image shows Fordow nuclear facility after massive bomb strike

items.description: Two months into a U.S.-led military campaign against Iran, American intelligence assessments indicate that the time Tehran would need to build a nuclear weapon has not shifted since last summer, when a joint U.S.-Israeli strike extended the timeline to roughly nine months to a year, Reuters reported on Monday, citing three sources familiar with the matter.[1][2]

items.title: Zelensky declares Ukraine ceasefire starting May 5-6

featured_image.name: Zelensky says Ukraine is ready for direct talks with Russia, but only after  a ceasefire

items.description:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky announced on Monday that Ukraine will observe a unilateral ceasefire beginning at midnight on the night of May 5-6, moving ahead without a formal agreement from Moscow. Writing on Telegram, Zelensky stated that Ukraine is proceeding because "human life is incomparably more valuable than the celebration of any anniversary," and that Ukraine will "act symmetrically" from the moment the ceasefire takes effect — echoing language he used during Ukraine's observance of an Orthodox Easter truce in April.[1][2]

The announcement comes hours after Russia's Defense Ministry declared its own two-day ceasefire for May 8-9 to coincide with the 81st anniversary of Victory Day, which commemorates the Soviet Union's defeat of Nazi Germany. The Kremlin said it did not require Ukraine's consent and threatened a "massive missile strike on the center of Kyiv" if Ukrainian forces attempted to disrupt the celebrations.[3][4]

items.title: Russia formally declares May 8-9 ceasefire in Ukraine for Victory Day

featured_image.name: Russia declares ceasefire with Ukraine on May 8-9 in honor of Victory Day

items.description: Russia's Defence Ministry announced on Monday that President Vladimir Putin has ordered a ceasefire in Ukraine on May 8-9 to mark the anniversary of the Soviet victory over Nazi Germany in World War Two. The declaration formalizes a proposal Putin first floated during a 90-minute phone call with U.S. President Donald Trump on April 29.[1][2][3][4]

items.title: Trump urges South Korea to join Hormuz mission after ship attack

featured_image.name: Trump Pressures South Korea, Japan on Strait of Hormuz Support

items.description: President Donald Trump has called on South Korea to participate in "Project Freedom," the U.S.-led naval operation to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, citing an attack on a South Korean cargo ship as grounds for Seoul's involvement. The renewed pressure on Monday came as the United States launched its effort to guide stranded commercial vessels through the contested waterway, escalating a months-long diplomatic push to draw allies into the Middle East conflict with Iran.

items.title: Putin retreating to bunkers amid coup and drone fears, EU intelligence report says

featured_image.name: As economic despair mounts, Russian official admits the country has had  enough of the war on Ukraine | Fortune

items.description:
Russian President Vladimir Putin has been spending extended periods in underground bunkers in southern Russia since March 2026, gripped by fears of both a coup by political elites and a drone-based assassination, according to reports published by the Financial Times and the independent Russian investigative outlet Istories (Important Stories), citing a classified European intelligence report.[1][2][3]

The revelations came as a Ukrainian drone struck a 52-story luxury residential tower on Mosfilmovskaya Street in Moscow overnight on May 4 — roughly six kilometers from the Kremlin — underscoring the aerial threats that have rattled the Russian leadership. Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin confirmed the strike on Telegram, saying there were no casualties. The attack occurred just five days before Russia's May 9 Victory Day parade, for which the defense ministry had already announced that military equipment and cadets would be absent from Red Square this year as a precaution against drone strikes.[4][5][6][7][8][9][10]

items.title: Iran threatens to attack ships as U.S. launches Project Freedom

featured_image.name: When will Strait of Hormuz be 'safe' for commercial shipping again?

items.description:
Oil prices rose sharply on Monday as Iran warned it would target any vessel attempting to transit the Strait of Hormuz without its authorization, escalating a confrontation with the United States over the critical waterway that has been effectively shut since the start of the U.S.-Iran war in late February.

Brent crude climbed more than 3 percent to around $112 per barrel and briefly topped $114 during the session, while West Texas Intermediate crude gained nearly 3 percent to approximately $105 per barrel, according to the Associated Press. The surge came as Iran directly challenged President Donald Trump's newly announced "Project Freedom," a military operation to escort stranded commercial ships out of the strait.[1][2]

items.title: UAE issues missile alert as Hormuz standoff intensifies

featured_image.name: The UAE Is Bolstering Its Formidable Air Defenses

items.description:
Residents in the United Arab Emirates received emergency mobile alerts on Monday warning of a potential missile threat, as explosions from air defense intercepts were heard over Dubai. The National Emergency Crisis and Disaster Management Authority (NCEMA) urged people to shelter in place and follow official channels, before issuing a follow-up message declaring the situation safe.[1][2]

The incident marks the first such alert since the US-Iran ceasefire was declared on April 8, and comes as tensions in the region have escalated sharply following President Donald Trump's announcement of "Project Freedom," a naval operation to guide stranded vessels through the Strait of Hormuz.[3][4]

items.title: CENTCOM denies Iran's claim of missile strike as Hormuz operation begins

featured_image.name: Iran fires missiles into Strait of Hormuz during military exercise as  nuclear talks begin | The Times of Israel

items.description: Iran said on Monday that it struck a U.S. Navy frigate with two missiles near the Strait of Hormuz, a claim swiftly denied by the U.S. military as President Donald Trump's high-stakes naval operation to reopen the waterway got underway. The dueling narratives underscored the volatility of a standoff that has choked off roughly a fifth of the world's oil and gas shipments for more than two months.
